quests.instruction: You open your bag at lunchtime and your lunchbox isn't there. What is the best step?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell your teacher or the office ☎️
options: Share a friend's lunch without asking 🍱
Skip lunch and say nothing about it 🙂
Tell your teacher or the office ☎️
quests.hint: Adults at school can solve this.
quests.explanation: Telling an adult lets the school find a solution, such as contacting your family or arranging a meal.
quests.funFact: Schools usually have a plan for students who forget lunch.

quests.instruction: Your teacher asked everyone to bring a ruler today, and yours is at home. What is a sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell your teacher and ask for a spare 📏
options: Tell your teacher and ask for a spare 📏
Quietly borrow a classmate's without asking 🫳
Sit out the activity and say nothing 🪑
quests.hint: Think about what keeps you able to take part.
quests.explanation: Asking to borrow a spare lets you take part, and next time you can check your bag the night before.
quests.funFact: Many teachers keep a few spare tools for these moments.

quests.instruction: It's reading time, but your book is at home. What is a good solution?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask your teacher for another book today 📚
options: Ask your teacher for another book today 📚
Sit and wait for the reading time to end ⏳
Take a classmate's book while they're away 🫳
quests.explanation: A different book means you can still practice reading instead of missing out.
quests.funFact: Adults read about 200 to 250 words a minute on average.

quests.instruction: A sign in the hallway says 'Rooms 10–15 →'. You need Room 12. Which way do you go?
quests.correctAnswer: Follow the arrow and look for room 12 ➡️
options: Go the opposite way along the hallway ⬅️
Walk to the end and turn back again 🔄
Follow the arrow and look for room 12 ➡️
quests.hint: Read the arrow and the numbers.
quests.explanation: Signs with arrows and numbers tell you where rooms are, so you can find your way.
quests.funFact: Rooms are often numbered in order along a hallway.

quests.instruction: You are on the ground floor, and the library is on the second floor. What should you use?
quests.correctAnswer: The stairs or the lift 🪜
options: The stairs or the lift 🪜
The playground steps 🛝
The ground-floor corridor 🚪
quests.explanation: Stairs or a lift connect floors. Take the stairs carefully, holding the rail.
quests.funFact: Lifts in schools are mostly for people who can't use stairs.

quests.instruction: You are lost in a big school building. What is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask a teacher or staff member 🙋
options: Ask a teacher or staff member 🙋
Go outside and look through the windows 🪟
Wander around until you spot the room 🚶
quests.explanation: Asking a staff member is the quickest and safest way to get where you need to go.
quests.funFact: Many schools have maps near the entrance.

quests.instruction: A yellow sign says 'Wet floor' in the hallway. What is the safest choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Walk slowly around it or use another way 🚶
options: Slide across it carefully on one foot 🛝
Walk slowly around it or use another way 🚶
Run across it quickly before it dries 🏃
quests.explanation: The sign warns of a slippery floor, so going around or walking slowly prevents falls.
quests.funFact: The yellow 'wet floor' sign is used in many countries.

quests.instruction: You open the door and someone is right behind it. What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Open it slowly and carefully 🚪
options: Pull it open and step through at once 🚶
Push it open fast to get through 💨
Open it slowly and carefully 🚪
quests.explanation: Opening slowly lets you see who is on the other side and avoids bumping them.
quests.funFact: Doors open toward the hall in many schools, so look first.

quests.instruction: You are carrying a sharp pencil, and you need to walk across the room. What is the safest way?
quests.correctAnswer: Hold it pointing down and walk carefully ✏️
options: Tuck it behind your ear while you hurry 🏃
Hold it pointing down and walk carefully ✏️
Carry it point-up so it won't poke your leg 🔼
quests.explanation: Holding a pencil point down keeps the sharp end away from faces.
quests.funFact: Pencil points are sharp enough to hurt, so they should point away from faces.

quests.instruction: Your friend moved away and you've felt sad for days. Who is a good person to talk to?
quests.correctAnswer: Teacher or counselor 💬
options: Teacher or counselor 💬
Cafeteria worker 🧑‍🍳
Bus driver 🚌
quests.hint: Think about who listens to feelings.
quests.explanation: Trusted adults at school can listen and help when someone is feeling sad for a while.
quests.funFact: It's normal to feel sad when a friend moves away.

quests.instruction: You notice a broken swing on the playground. Who should you tell?
quests.correctAnswer: The teacher on playground duty 🙋
options: Only your classmates in the playground 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
Nobody; someone else will tell them 🤷
The teacher on playground duty 🙋
quests.hint: Adults can block it off or fix it.
quests.explanation: Telling an adult stops others from using the broken swing and gets it repaired.
quests.funFact: Playground equipment is usually checked regularly for loose parts.

quests.instruction: The bus you normally take home hasn't come, and it's getting late. Who do you tell?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a teacher or the school office 🙋
options: Wait for a stranger to give you a ride 🚗
Tell a teacher or the school office 🙋
Walk home alone 🚶
quests.explanation: School staff can contact your family and arrange a safe way home.
quests.funFact: Schools usually have a plan for transport problems.

quests.instruction: Tomorrow your class visits a museum. Which group of items is the most useful?
quests.correctAnswer: Water bottle, notebook, pencil, hat 🎒
options: Skateboard, football, torch, comic 🛹
Water bottle, notebook, pencil, hat 🎒
Paintbrush, glue, dictionary, apron 🖌️
quests.hint: Think about walking, looking, and noting.
quests.explanation: On a museum trip you walk, drink water, and note things you learn.
quests.funFact: Many museums let you draw in notebooks but not use pens.

quests.instruction: Your class has a gardening lesson outside. What should you bring or wear?
quests.correctAnswer: Old clothes, gloves, and a water bottle 🧤
options: Old clothes, gloves, and a water bottle 🧤
A white dress, sandals, and a clutch bag 👗
Your best uniform and polished shoes 👔
quests.explanation: Old clothes and gloves protect you from dirt, and water keeps you hydrated.
quests.funFact: Gloves help protect hands from thorns and soil.

quests.instruction: It's sports day, and the sun is hot. Which items should you pack?
quests.correctAnswer: Hat, water bottle, sports shoes 🧢
options: Umbrella, raincoat, and rubber boots ☔
Hat, water bottle, sports shoes 🧢
Notebook, ruler, and a glue stick 📏
quests.explanation: A hat shields you from the sun, water keeps you cool, and sports shoes keep your feet safe.
quests.funFact: Sun protection matters even on cloudy days.

quests.instruction: You leave the cap off the glue stick. What will probably happen?
quests.correctAnswer: It will dry out and stop working 🧴
options: It will dry out and stop working 🧴
It will get stronger and last longer 💪
It will stay fresh for a whole year 📅
quests.explanation: Air dries out the glue, so keep caps on to make it last.
quests.funFact: Many glue sticks have a cap to keep air out.

quests.instruction: You leave your bag in the aisle. What could happen?
quests.correctAnswer: Someone might trip over it 🎒
options: The aisle will be a little quieter 🤫
Someone might trip over it 🎒
It will stay perfectly safe there 🙂
quests.explanation: A bag in the walkway is a tripping hazard, so keep aisles clear.
quests.funFact: Clear walkways matter especially in emergencies.

quests.instruction: You keep a library book long after it is due. What happens?
quests.correctAnswer: Other readers have to wait for it 📚
options: The book becomes yours after a week 🏠
Other readers have to wait for it 📚
The librarian buys another copy for you 📖
quests.explanation: A book that stays out is missing from the shelf, and libraries have rules to ensure sharing.
quests.funFact: Many libraries let you renew a book if nobody else is waiting.

quests.instruction: You have 10 minutes left and three questions to do. What is a smart approach?
quests.correctAnswer: Do the ones you know first ⏱️
options: Leave them blank and wait for the bell 📄
Spend all ten minutes on the hardest one 🐢
Do the ones you know first ⏱️
quests.explanation: Answering what you know first earns the most progress, and you can try the rest with the time left.
quests.funFact: Skipping a hard question and coming back is a good test strategy.

quests.instruction: The bell will ring in two minutes, and your game isn't finished. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Start wrapping up and tidy your things 🧹
options: Start a brand-new game with friends 🎲
Hide away so you can keep playing 🙂
Start wrapping up and tidy your things 🧹
quests.explanation: Finishing up early lets you stop on time and not rush.
quests.funFact: Timers and alarms can count down to remind you when time is almost up.

quests.instruction: Your bus arrives in five minutes, and you're still packing. Which item must you be sure to take?
quests.correctAnswer: Your diary and homework 📔
options: The pencil sharpener ✏️
Your old drawings 🖼️
Your diary and homework 📔
quests.explanation: Homework and diary matter for tomorrow, so pack them first.
quests.funFact: Packing in order of importance means you won't leave behind what counts.

quests.instruction: You spill paint on the floor. What is the best first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell your teacher and help clean it up 🧽
options: Tell your teacher and help clean it up 🧽
Spread it out so it's hard to notice 🙂
Walk away before anyone sees 🚶
quests.explanation: Telling the teacher and helping clean keeps the floor safe and shows responsibility.
quests.funFact: Wet paint on a floor can be slippery.

quests.instruction: You told a classmate the wrong page number, and they've started the wrong exercise. What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell them the right page, say sorry 🙏
options: Tell them the right page, say sorry 🙏
Tell them it was their fault 👈
Hope they don't notice 🙈
quests.hint: Own up and put it right.
quests.explanation: Correcting the mistake quickly and apologizing helps your classmate and shows responsibility.
quests.funFact: Page numbers became common after the printing press spread across Europe.

quests.instruction: You think you left your pencil case on the bus. What is a good thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask your teacher to check the office 🙋
options: Ask your teacher to check the office 🙋
Decide it's gone and stop looking 😢
Borrow a classmate's case tomorrow 🫳
quests.explanation: School staff can check lost property or ask the driver.
quests.funFact: Labels with your name help lost items get returned.

quests.instruction: A worksheet says, 'Circle the biggest number.' What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Draw a ring around the biggest number ⭕
options: Underline the smallest number you see ➖
Cross out every number that's too small ❌
Draw a ring around the biggest number ⭕
quests.explanation: Reading the verb carefully (circle, underline, cross out) tells you exactly what to do.
quests.funFact: Worksheets often use words like 'circle', 'tick', and 'match'.

quests.instruction: Instructions say, 'Complete all questions on both sides of the page.' What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Turn the page over and keep going 🔄
options: Stop at the bottom of the front 🛑
Turn the page over and keep going 🔄
Choose only the easy ones 🍃
quests.explanation: 'Both sides' means the back counts too, so check before handing it in.
quests.funFact: Looking at the back of a page is an easy way to miss work.

quests.instruction: The instruction says, 'Work with a partner and share one idea each.' What must happen?
quests.correctAnswer: Both partners add an idea 🤝
options: The pair shares one idea together 👥
Both partners add an idea 🤝
One partner gives two ideas 🗣️
quests.explanation: 'One idea each' means both partners contribute.
quests.funFact: Words like 'each' mean every person.

quests.instruction: Your teacher writes, 'Check your capital letters,' on your work. What do you do next?
quests.correctAnswer: Look back and fix the capital letters ✏️
options: Rub out the teacher's note and move on 🧽
Rewrite everything in a different pen 🖊️
Look back and fix the capital letters ✏️
quests.hint: Feedback tells you what to improve.
quests.explanation: Reading and using feedback helps your work get better each time.
quests.funFact: Using feedback is one of the quickest ways to improve.

quests.instruction: Your teacher says, 'Great start! Add one more detail.' What is the next step?
quests.correctAnswer: Add another detail to your work 📝
options: Hand it in as it is right now 📥
Start again from the very beginning 🆕
Add another detail to your work 📝
quests.explanation: The teacher likes your start and wants you to build on it.
quests.funFact: Adding details often means answering who, what, where, or why.

quests.instruction: Your teacher says, 'Slow down and read the question twice.' How does this help?
quests.correctAnswer: You understand what the question is asking 🔍
options: You are given more questions to answer 📚
You understand what the question is asking 🔍
You finish the paper much more quickly ⚡
quests.explanation: Reading carefully helps you answer the question that was actually asked.
quests.funFact: Rushing can lead to mistakes even when you know the answer.
